*   **Member Name:** Quinn Carter

*   **Reference Number:** POC-698F4692AE-97118

*   **Requested Service:** Total Knee Replacement (Left/Right/Bilateral - [Insert lateral side, e.g., Left])
*   **Procedure Code:** CPT 27447
*   **Requesting Surgeon:** Dr. Lindqvist, MD

Dear Aetna Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal Aetna’s denial of the prior authorization request for my total knee replacement (CPT 27447), which was submitted by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist. The denial letter dated August 12, 2026, states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is clinically incorrect and directly contradicted by my medical records. My records document not only a severe, advanced joint disease but also an extensive, 14-week formal trial of conservative care that completely satisfies—and in fact exceeds—the criteria set forth in **Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) 0660: Knee Arthroplasty**.

Below, I have mapped my clinical records directly to the medical necessity criteria required under Aetna CPB 0660.

### 1. Documented Trial of Conservative Treatment (Addressing the Denial Reason)
Aetna CPB 0660 states that members must have a:
> "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/body mass index (BMI)) that is clearly addressed in the medical record"

The policy further clarifies in Footnote 1:
> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy; activities of daily living (ADLs) diminished despite completing a plan of care)..."

My medical record documents that I have fully met and exhausted these requirements:
*   **Duration of Conservative Care:** I completed a **14-week trial** of supervised physical therapy (exceeding the standard 12-week requirement) from **March 18, 2026, to June 24, 2026**, consisting of **20 completed in-person visits** with a licensed physical therapist. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Type of Physical Therapy:** The supervised therapy focused directly on "flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises," specifically quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.
*   **Medication Management:** I utilized prescribed NSAIDs (anti-inflammatory medications) for **4 months** (approximately 16 weeks), which provided inadequate relief. 
*   **Therapeutic Injection:** I received a therapeutic intra-articular corticosteroid injection on **March 28, 2026**, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. *(Note: This injection was administered more than 12 weeks prior to my planned surgery, satisfying the policy's safety window).*
*   **Diminished ADLs Despite Therapy:** Despite completing this comprehensive plan of care, my activities of daily living remain severely diminished, and my symptoms are unresolved.
*   **No Morbid Obesity:** My BMI is 29, which is well below the relative contraindication threshold of 40 (morbid obesity). 
*   *[If patient age is under 50, insert: "Although I am under 50 years of age, which Aetna notes as a relative contraindication, I have fully exhausted all non-surgical treatment options as outlined above, and my condition qualifies for immediate surgical intervention due to severe bone-on-bone articulation as discussed below."] [If patient age is 50 or older, insert: "Because I am over 50 years of age and my BMI is 29, I have no relative contraindications, and my 14-week trial of conservative therapy fully satisfies the 12-week policy requirement."]*

### 2. Exception for Bone-on-Bone Articulation
Aetna CPB 0660 explicitly recognizes that:
> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral) or severe angular deformity..."

My diagnostic imaging from **July 6, 2026** (weight-bearing knee radiographs) demonstrates:
*   **Severe Osteoarthritis:** Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis.
*   **Bone-on-Bone Articulation:** Structural bone-on-bone apposition in the weight-bearing medial compartment, as well as the patellofemoral compartment, and lateral joint-space narrowing.
*   **Severe Angular Deformity:** Physical examination reveals a structural **varus alignment** (bowed leg) of the knee joint.

Under Aetna's own policy, because I exhibit Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 severe osteoarthritis with weight-bearing bone-on-bone articulation and varus deformity, an extensive conservative trial was technically clinically inappropriate. However, I still completed and failed a comprehensive 14-week trial.

### 3. Severe Pain, Physical Findings, and Functional Impairment
Aetna CPB 0660 requires "advanced joint disease demonstrated by" pain and functional disability interfering with ADLs, along with specific physical examination findings. My records document:
*   **Symptom Duration and Severity:** 24 months of progressive, severe, and unrelenting knee pain that is unrelieved by rest.
*   **Severe ADL Limitations:** I am unable to climb stairs without assistance, and my severe pain wakes me 3 to 4 times every night.
*   **Objective Physical Exam Findings:** Physical examination by Dr. Lindqvist documents a restricted and painful range of motion (5 to 100 degrees), joint crepitus, and joint effusion (swelling).
*   **Absence of Contraindications:** My records confirm I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker.

### Conclusion and Request for Reversal
The prior authorization packet submitted by Dr. Lindqvist contains the physical therapy discharge notes confirming 14 weeks/20 visits of in-person PT, clinical notes detailing 4 months of NSAID use, and the July 6, 2026, X-ray report demonstrating Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 bone-on-bone arthritis. 

Every single criterion required for the medical necessity of a total knee arthroplasty under Aetna CPB 0660 has been met and thoroughly documented. I request that Aetna immediately reverse this denial and approve the requested total knee replacement so that I may proceed with this medically necessary surgery.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Quinn Carter
Member ID: W142538049
